findings.text: The `kode` row emits no non-interactive switch, so a launch composes `kode [--model M] <directive>` while RESEARCH-2's step-2 table (which the spec's "Use RESEARCH-2's step-2 table" item tells the author to follow) documents headless Kode as `kode -p "<prompt>"`: the cited parser says "-p, --print ... Print response and exit (useful for pipes)." Without `-p` Kode starts its interactive TUI, so the run only ends at the watchdog `--timeout` and records `agent-timeout`. `Args` (or `PromptFlag`) must carry `-p`; the row's argv expectation at internal/core/run/agents_internal_test.go:237-238 repeats the omission, and docs/manual.md documents the same flagless invocation, so both pass over the defect.

The `neovate` row emits no non-interactive switch, so a launch composes `neovate [--model M] <directive>` while RESEARCH-2's step-2 table documents `neovate -q "<prompt>"` and the cited source says "Run the code agent with a prompt, interactive by default, use -q/--quiet for non-interactive mode." A launch therefore opens the Neovate TUI and only ends when the watchdog kills it (`agent-timeout`). `Args` needs `-q`; the argv expectation at internal/core/run/agents_internal_test.go:247-250 encodes the same omission and cannot catch it.

The `qoder` row emits no non-interactive switch, so a launch composes `qoder [--model M] <directive>` while the cited reference says "To enter Headless mode, add the --print flag (short form -p)" and RESEARCH-2's step-2 table gives `qoder -p "<prompt>"`. Without `-p` the CLI stays interactive and the run hangs until the watchdog records `agent-timeout`. `Args` needs `-p`; the argv expectation at internal/core/run/agents_internal_test.go:277-280 and the manual row repeat the omission.

The `qodercn` row emits no non-interactive switch, so a launch composes `qodercn [--model M] <directive>` while the cited Chinese reference says headless mode is entered with `--print` (short `-p`) and RESEARCH-2's step-2 table gives `qodercn -p "<prompt>"`. Without `-p` the run only ends at the watchdog timeout (`agent-timeout`). `Args` needs `-p`; internal/core/run/agents_internal_test.go:283-286 encodes the same omission.

The spec's "Record the probe in `launcher.json`: `probe: {args, ok}`" holds only on the one-shot path: `repairLoop` (internal/core/run/repair.go:77) builds its own `launcher` record with no `Probe`, and `invoke` probes before it branches into `--rounds`. So `run --agent fx --rounds 2` passes the probe, launches, and rewrites `launcher.json` with no `probe` field. Setting `Probe: args.probe` in the repair record closes the gap; no test covers a probed row together with `--rounds`, so it is invisible.

A parent-context cancel during the probe is folded into the timeout arm: `pctx.Err() != nil` is true for `context.Canceled`, so an operator Ctrl-C while the identity probe runs refuses `agent-mismatch` with the result "timed out" instead of the launcher's `canceled` code, which the rest of the launcher prefers whenever `ctx.Err() != nil`. Distinguish `context.DeadlineExceeded` from a canceled parent before blaming the binary.

A missing commander is a wiring failure, but the probe types it as `agent-mismatch` with a message about the binary and the operator-facing hint then tells the user to fix their settings.json binary path; `spawn()` treats the same condition as an internal error (`errNoCommander`, service.go:668). An internal nil-commander refusal should not be typed as the agent-identity mismatch.

The test comment promises a two-way pin ("a name in the docs that no row answers is a lie"), but `assertSurfaceNames` only walks the names scanned out of `agents.go` and looks each one up in the surface; a stale or misspelled agent name left in usage.go, docs/manual.md or references/commands.md is never checked, so the documented-name-with-no-row case the comment claims to catch still passes.
findings.quote: // docs is undiscoverable; a name in the docs that no row answers is a lie.

findings.text: An operator row that sets `probe_match` without `probe_args` (or with `probe_args: []`) is accepted silently: `probe()` returns early when `len(ProbeArgs) == 0`, so the identity check the operator asked for never runs and nothing warns. Only the `probe_args`-without-`probe_match` direction refuses, so the pair validation is one-sided.

The usage.go half of the new guard is a bare substring search over the whole file: usage.go contains `pa` (in `package main`) and `pi` (in `pipeline`), so deleting one of those names from the `--agent` list still satisfies `strings.Contains` and the test passes. Match the list shape (the `<...|...>` run) instead of searching the file for the bare name.
